text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Rural Union wants to dismiss Uno Mereste from the council of the Bank of Estonia, declaring him responsible for the mistakes of the central bank.
- Mayor of Tallinn Robert Lepikson says he is considering suing daily Eesti Paevaleht for an offensive editorial in the paper.
- Russia has asked for Finland's help in solving the country's disagreements with Estonia. The proposal did not involve mediation, the Finnish Foreign Ministry stressed.
- Police are looking for Imre Tali an officer of the traffic police from Harju county who is suspected of murder, officials said.
- The Government supports the plan of Tartu University to apply for a $10 million loan from the World Bank, prime minister Mart Siimann said.
- The police department violated the law on procurement for state institutions when they bought two expensive Nissan jeeps, the state inspection said.
- Estonian Union Bank will make its first move in the Russian market when it signs founding documents with United Russian Leasing next week in St.Petersburg, leaders of the bank said.
- An Estonian ship, the Merkuur, sank in the Latvian port of Ventspils yesterday soon after the ship reached the port in need of urgent repairs. The crew was not hurt.
- Police in Finland and Sweden fear that Estonia is developing into an amphetamine-producing state.
- US firm CHS has bought the wholesale division of the Estonian computer company Microlink.
